facts.statement: Latoplatecarpus is an extinct genus of mosasaur.
The genus Latoplatecarpus was named by Konishi and Caldwell in 2011.
Fossils of Latoplatecarpus have been found in the northern Gulf of Mexico, the Western Interior Basin of North America, and the Saratov Region of Russia.
facts.quote: known from the Late Cretaceous (early middle Campanian stage) of the northern Gulf of Mexico, the Western Interior Basin of North America, and a singular specimen from the Saratov Region, of Russia.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was collected from the Pembina Member of the Pierre Shale in southern Manitoba, dating to about 80.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype was collected in the Pembina Mountain, in southern Manitoba, from the Pembina Member of the Pierre Shale, dating to the early middle Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous period, about 80.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: The holotype of L. willistoni consists of a nearly complete skull with the mandible and dentary, plus a partial postcranial skeleton.
facts.quote: L. willistoni is known from the holotype TMP 84.162.01, a nearly complete skull, including the mandible and dentary, and a partial postcranial skeleton.

facts.statement: Subsequent authors have challenged the placement of L. nichollsae in Latoplatecarpus and reassigned it back to the genus Plioplatecarpus.
facts.quote: The interpretation of L. nichollsae as a species of Latoplatecarpus was challenged by subsequent authors, who have reassigned the species back to Plioplatecarpus.

facts.statement: Latoplatecarpus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 80 to 75 million years ago.
facts.quote: Latoplatecarpus es un género extinto de mosasáurido plioplatecarpino que vivió en el Cretácico Superior (hace ~80-75 millones de años a principios del Campaniense.

facts.statement: Latoplatecarpus was a medium-sized aquatic predator, reaching lengths of 5 to 6 meters.
facts.quote: fue un depredador acuático de tamaño medio (5-6 m de largo)

facts.statement: A study of mosasaur materials from the Campanian Rybushka Formation in Beloe Ozero, Russia, identified Latoplatecarpus as the only identifiable plioplatecarpine genus.
facts.quote: El estudio de materiales de mosasaurios de la Formación Rybushka del Campaniense de la localidad de Beloe Ozero (región de Saratov, Rusia) reveló que el único taxón de plioplatecarpino identificable a nivel de género es Latoplatecarpus.

facts.statement: The discovery of Latoplatecarpus in Russia demonstrates that the genus had a significantly wider geographic and stratigraphic distribution than previously known.
facts.quote: El primer registro de Latoplatecarpus fuera de Norteamérica demuestra que este género tuvo una distribución geográfica y estratigráfica significativamente más amplia.

facts.statement: Latoplatecarpus belongs to the family Mosasauridae.
Latoplatecarpus is classified within the subfamily Plioplatecarpinae.
The time range for Latoplatecarpus is the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Latoplatecarpus belongs to the tribe Plioplatecarpini.
